rv.q: A People stands out as essential summertime theater, honoring its deep historical foundations while resonating powerfully with contemporary audiences.
But I came away from the evening not really understanding what the underlying message is.
But more often than not, the production is done in by the rough edges of the vignettes.
This presentation of short scenes, stories, songs, passages told partly in Yiddish, and using a couple puppets and masks, is much more confusing than it is enlightening.
While the cast was, for the most part, highly talented, and some of the vignettes cute, I truly felt that this is still a play in development...
To achieve this worthy goal, the piece would benefit from thoughtful use of the scissors and the pen; it’s got all it needs to be a more rewarding experience…just not quite yet.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Jewish history mosaic, praising its ambitious scope and extraordinary ensemble work while finding the sprawling 5000-year narrative confusing and overstuffed with disparate elements.
